clue.text: Someone like you, living around kinky vice, runs place in Indonesia

indicators.note: around says the word for living wraps round everything that follows

parts.note: to earn a crust is to make a living, so a crust is a living

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of vice are bent into a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
Bali is an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: A shady expat in Indonesia, steeped in vice, runs a dubious establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone like you' addresses the person solving the puzzle; 'kinky' scrambles vice, and 'around' has the living word enclose it with the runs and island pieces. To earn a crust is British for making a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone doing this puzzle is a crossword enthusiast, which is what the word means.

clue.text: Bedroom feature, artists' bust?

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'drawers' as people who draw: the chest belonging to artists.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom cabinet with drawers is the standard furniture item; the second reading is a pun on drawers as sketchers.

explanation.surface: Lively women dressed only in their underwear, one in four of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Undines are female water spirits of folklore, so spirited females is a pun on their nature.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun; it is the adjective, unyielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that will not stretch or give is rigid, as firm means here.

ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for always, as in for ever and ay

explanation.surface: A Munich team has always put money into a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayern Munich is the German football club, a side in sports terms.

clue.text: Proper extract executed?

parts.note: to elicit is to draw out or extract

explanation.surface: Was taking out that proper extract an execution?
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means lawful, permitted, which is proper in the legal sense.

clue.text: Tongue is holding fruit up with half of lips

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the combined piece is read bottom to top
holding says the word is wraps round the fruit

parts.note: a haw is the fruit of the hawthorn

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of lips

explanation.surface: Someone's tongue is lifting fruit to their mouth with half their lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' means language here, not the body part; 'holding' and 'up' act on 'is' and the fruit together, so the whole wrapped piece is read upwards before half of lips follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language, and this is a Bantu language of East Africa.

parts.note: Lara is a girl's name

a trike is a tricycle

clue.text: Break down going round this roundabout with swerving movement

indicators.note: going round says the breakdown word encircles the jumbled piece

parts.note: to fail is to break down

indicators.note: roundabout means in a winding way, so the letters of this are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car breaking down on a roundabout and swerving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like a traffic junction in the surface but jumbles this, and 'going round' has the breakdown word encircle the result. A fishtail is a car's rear end sliding.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle whose back end slides side to side is making a sideways swerve of this kind.

clue.text: Old poser showing bit of leg accepting money for kiss

clue.text: Like mistletoe, it is a hit when put up, caught underneath

in a down clue put up means the phrase reads from bottom to top

explanation.walkthrough: 'when put up' turns ITISARAP into PARASITI; 'underneath' puts C after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe grows on and feeds from host trees, so it lives in that dependent way.

explanation.definitionFit: Grace and decency both mean seemly, proper behaviour.

clue.text: Order ranks Abe Lincoln here

clue.text: Fruitcake's quality was keeping cows in gas

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Don't kill when angry

explanation.definitionFit: To spare someone is to let them live; going spare is British slang for being furious.

clue.text: Aren't breaks in payment inward looking?

explanation.definitionFit: A re-entrant angle points inwards, so it faces or looks inward.

clue.text: Said to be on drugs in a pitiful state, though not proven
